identification.name: Stainless Steel 17-7 PH (Condition TH1050)
identification.common_form_notes: Supplied in the solution-annealed Condition A for forming/machining, then conditioned and aged by the end user to reach the properties shown here — an extra step versus 17-4 PH. 17-7 PH is semi-austenitic: unlike 17-4 PH (martensitic even in the annealed state), Condition A 17-7 PH is largely austenite and must first be "conditioned" (a thermal or mechanical treatment that transforms the retained austenite to martensite) before the final aging step can precipitation-harden it. TH1050 uses thermal conditioning (heating to a high temperature, then cooling) followed by aging at 1050°F (565°C); the alternative conditions RH950 (subzero/refrigeration conditioning + 950°F age, higher strength/lower ductility) and CH900 (cold-work conditioning + 900°F age, highest strength) trade ductility for strength versus TH1050.
identification.notes: A precipitation-hardening stainless chosen for high strength with better formability than 17-4 PH during the pre-hardened (Condition A) state, at the cost of a more involved heat-treatment sequence (conditioning + aging, vs. 17-4 PH's single aging step). TH1050 was chosen as the representative condition — the standard, most commonly specified general-purpose temper, analogous to how H1025 was chosen for the 17-4 PH entry in this database, balancing strength and ductility better than the higher-strength RH950/CH900 conditions. Elongation is reported as a range (3.0–7.0%) rather than a single typical value; stored as min/max with no typical figure. Shear strength derived via von Mises: UTS (ultimate tensile strength)/√3 = 1240/1.732 ≈ 716 MPa (appropriate here, unlike the brittle ceramic/cermet entries in this database, since this is a standard ductile hardened stainless with normal dislocation-slip yielding behavior). Melting point is solidus (1400°C); liquidus is 1450°C. Electrical conductivity (2.08% IACS (International Annealed Copper Standard)) derived from the source's stated resistivity (83.0 µΩ·cm). Ferromagnetic — like 17-4 PH, the final aged condition is predominantly martensitic.

typical_usage: High-strength, formable stainless parts where the material must be shaped in a softer state before final hardening: springs, fasteners, diaphragms, and aerospace structural components needing a good strength/corrosion-resistance/formability balance. Choose over 17-4 PH when better cold-formability in the pre-hardened state matters; choose 17-4 PH instead for a simpler single-step aging process without the semi-austenitic conditioning step. Like 17-4 PH, costs noticeably more than 303/304/316 and needs post-fabrication heat treatment — only worth the extra process complexity when a part must both be formed and reach hardened-steel strength levels.
